messages:
joel: Quick question — we need a decision on how to show prefetch/cache savings in the SLA-aware cost dashboard. My rough idea: attribute prefetch savings to models that consumed the prefetched tokens within a session window, amortized by token usage. Pros: aligns with who benefited. Cons: cross-tenant prefetching and cold-start credits complicate it. Thoughts?
ana: do you mean session window per API key or per request trace? both implications matter. if per API key, a noisy tenant could absorb others' prefetchs.
sam: quick flag: sampling will bias this. we sample 1% of requests for detailed traces; if we attribute based on sampled traces we might over/under-estimate savings for tail tenants. need correction factor.
maria: agree with Sam. Also need to expose whether savings column is "estimated" or "attributed". console UX should make the confidence visible. maybe an uncertainty % or sample rate badge. :bar_chart:
lee: another heuristic — attribute by downstream token consumption in the next N requests from the same session id. like: if prefetched keys saved 300 tokens and model A used 200 tokens and model B used 100 tokens, split 2:1. avoids per-key owner issues.
joel: that matches my thinking. Implementation question: do we do attribution in real-time or as a batch job? real-time allows live dashboards but is heavier. batch overnight is easier and reduces noise smoothing.
nana: for SLA math we need near-real-time for billing alerts. maybe two layers: a near-real-time estimate (approx) and a delayed authoritative number for invoices.
sam: +1. For canaries/rollouts we must ensure we don't credit canary trials with full savings. add rule: if model variant is canary flag, attribute only to baseline unless rollout % > threshold.
maria: telemetry note: we need a deterministic join key. current traces have request_id and session_id; use session_id when present, fallback to hashed api_key + 1min window. document this clearly.
lee: SQL sketch for nightly attribution job:
```
WITH prefetchs AS (SELECT session_id, prefetch_id, saved_tokens FROM prefetch_events WHERE ts >= date_sub(now(), interval 1 day)),
consumed AS (SELECT session_id, model_id, SUM(tokens) as used_tokens FROM request_tokens WHERE ts >= date_sub(now(), interval 1 day) GROUP BY session_id, model_id),
split AS (SELECT p.prefetch_id, c.model_id, p.saved_tokens * (c.used_tokens / SUM(c.used_tokens) OVER (PARTITION BY p.prefetch_id)) as attributed_tokens FROM prefetchs p JOIN consumed c USING (session_id))
INSERT INTO nightly_attribution(prefetch_id, model_id, attributed_tokens) SELECT prefetch_id, model_id, SUM(attributed_tokens) FROM split GROUP BY prefetch_id, model_id;
```
joel: nice. we should also persist metadata: sample_rate_used, attribution_method_version, and a per-row confidence score.
nana: UX: add a toggle in the cost dashboard settings: "Attribution policy: token-proportional / owner-first / session-split" + description. default token-proportional.
sam: we also need a guardrail: if total attributed_tokens > saved_tokens (float rounding + double-counting bugs), cap to saved_tokens and emit alert. add an automatic reconciliation job.
maria: for telemetry sampling correction, we can use Horvitz-Thompson estimator to correct estimates from sampled traces. I can sketch that in RFC.
joel: action items: Maria to draft estimator appendix, Lee to prototype nightly SQL, Ana to mock console toggle copy, Sam to add canary rule to rollout docs. I'll open an RFC. dev-bot: created rfc/000-prefetch-attribution.md (link: https://r.rw/r/000-prefetch-attribution).
dev-bot: deploy: attribution-service v0.3 pushed to staging at 2025-11-02T12:02Z.
lee: pinging infra — we may need an extra scheduler slot for nightly job once this lands.
nana: marking for product review too — SLA implications.
sam: small nit: name the metric prefetched_token_savings and attributed_prefetch_savings to avoid confusion in dashboards.
joel: agreed. I'll include metric names in RFC. thanks everyone — we'll sync in the RFC thread and aim for a prototype by end of sprint.
